<p class="cs-lead">For advertising on Google Hotel Ads, travel marketplaces (like Expedia, Hotels.com, Booking.com) have to decide what to bid (how much to pay) for a click (CPC) on each unit of their inventory (biddable units).<br>
Pay too little and the ad gets outbid and never shows up; pay too much and the bookings don't pay back.</p>

<p class="cs-scale-intro">Imagine the scale of operations:</p>
<ul class="cs-scale">
  <li>~500K hotels across the globe</li>
  <li>~30 (major) markets</li>
  <li>3 devices (desktop, mobile, tablet)</li>
  <li>Length of stay, booking window, placement</li>
</ul>
<p class="cs-scale-total">The combination results in tens of billions of unique biddable combinations.</p>

<div class="cs-tiles">
  <div class="cs-tile">
<b>Billions</b><span>of unique bid-units</span></div>
  <div class="cs-tile">
<b>Daily</b><span>bid-update operations</span></div>
  <div class="cs-tile">
<b>ROAS constraints</b><span>Return target held across the portfolio, within business limits</span></div>
</div>

<h2 id="the-problem-statement">The problem statement</h2>
<p>Google Hotel Ads shows a ranked list of booking sites next to each hotel in its search results. Advertisers pay per click, and the bid largely decides where they appear.</p>

<p>For every bid unit <math display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> (a hotel × market × device × stay × dates combination), choose a bid <math display="inline"><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></math>:</p>
<p><math display="block"><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"></mtd><mtd columnalign="left"><munder><mo>max</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">{</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">}</mo></mrow></munder><mspace width="0.278em"></mspace><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>u</mi></munder><mi>Rev</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"></mtd><mtd columnalign="left"><mtext mathvariant="normal">subject to</mtext><mspace width="1.0em"></mspace><mfrac><mrow><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>u</mi></munder><mi>Rev</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>u</mi></munder><mi>Cost</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.278em"></mspace><mo>≥</mo><mspace width="0.278em"></mspace><mi>T</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></math></p>
<p>where:</p>
<ul>
<li><math display="inline"><mrow><mi>Rev</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></math>: Revenue estimate when bid is set to <math display="inline"><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></math></li>
<li><math display="inline"><mrow><mi>Cost</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></math>: Cost estimate when bid is set to <math display="inline"><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></math></li>
<li><math display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math>: ROAS target across the portfolio.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="complexity-involved">Complexity involved</h3>
<p>Google doesn’t take one unique bid-value per combination. Bids live in an account → campaign → ad group → hotel-group hierarchy.</p>
<ul>
<li>A base bid for each hotel, and multipliers for market, device, length of stay and dates set higher up and shared across many hotels.</li>
<li>Accounts also cap how many campaigns and ad groups they can hold.</li>
<li>So the task isn’t only to find the right price for billions of combinations; it’s to express those prices through a structure with far fewer controls.</li>
</ul>

<ul class="cs-why">
  <li><i class="bi bi-grid-3x3-gap"></i><span><b>Billions of decisions:</b> a daily price for every hotel, market and device, far beyond what anyone can set by hand.</span></li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-hourglass-split"></i><span><b>Sparse, slow feedback:</b> most hotels get few clicks, and bookings arrive days after the click.</span></li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-arrow-repeat"></i><span><b>The bid shapes its own data:</b> you only learn about the positions your own bids reach.</span></li>
  <li><i class="bi bi-people"></i><span><b>A crowded auction:</b> rivals, including sister brands, bid for the same hotels and react to every move.</span></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="bidding-model-evolution">Bidding Model Evolution</h2>
<p>Bidding started as rules maintained in spreadsheets. It then moved to automated, value-based bids; then to learned groupings, so hotels with little data could borrow from similar ones; then to models that predicted value and cost, with bids and multipliers optimised daily against the target. Later work explored reinforcement learning. Every new version had to beat the one in place in a live A/B test before it took over.</p>
<div class="cs-steps">
  <div><small>Rules</small><b>Spreadsheet rules</b></div>
  <div><small>Rules</small><b>Value-based automation</b></div>
  <div><small>ML</small><b>Learned groupings</b></div>
  <div><small>ML</small><b>Prediction Models + optimisation</b></div>
  <div class="later"><small>ML</small><b>Reinforcement learning</b></div>
</div>

<h2 id="my-role-and-outcomes">My Role and Outcomes</h2>
<div class="cs-result">
<p>The brand moved from 3rd–4th to a steady 2nd in click share ranking on the channel, while holding its return target (All while the channel revenue grew ~9x in 3 years).</p>
</div>
<div class="cs-boxes">
  <div class="cs-box">
    <h3>My role</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Owned bidding science and operations for the channel</li>
      <li>Led the development of 3 model iterations, from value-based automation to prediction-driven bidding</li>
      <li>Owned the optimisation layer of the prediction-driven system, a team effort</li>
      <li>Moved the daily pipeline onto the company’s ML platform</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="cs-box sand">
    <h3>Trade-offs</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Speed into the market vs tight control of the return target</li>
      <li>Pooling sparse hotels vs precision for each one</li>
      <li>Guard rails on bid changes vs freedom for the model</li>
      <li>A system the team can run vs a cleverer one that’s harder to operate</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="cs-box ink">
    <h3>Takeaways</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Operating cost is part of the model</li>
      <li>Every challenger earns its place in a live test</li>
      <li>Where data is thin, learn on purpose</li>
      <li>The same shape appears wherever a budget meets sparse, delayed outcomes</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
